description.narrative: Reporting is an important management tool which is used to inform relevant government officials and other stakeholders about the results being achieved by individual projects and the programme as a whole. For project partners, it is compulsory to use the prescribed Orange Knowledge annual report format in order to report on project achievements. The annual report also provides valuable data on the financial situation of the project. Based on an analysis of the project performance in relation to the project output(s) and expected outcome(s), a revision of the project work plan may be suggested by the project partners. The consequences of a possible revision on the project work plan and budget must be made clear in the annual report. Nuffic monitors outputs and outcomes and not activities. Therefore, the main focus of the annual report must be on the achievement of the project’s output(s) and planned outcome(s). The information provided in the annual reports of the projects is used by Nuffic to monitor the progress of the project and to inform the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and other stakeholders about the output(s) and outcome(s) being achieved by individual projects and the Orange Knowledge programme as a whole. Please note that if project progress is in accordance with the original planning, reporting requirements are minimal. Only in case of deviations from the planning, more elaboration is demanded. In the Grant Obligations and Conditions, the obligatory dates for submission of the annual/additional reports are mentioned. The final report must reflect on the entire project period.

title.narrative: 2. Project progress and achievement

description.narrative:
In this section (maximum 1000 words), please
**For TMT+:**
Comment to what extent the outputs have been achieved. Comment on the activities that have taken place and the most important milestones.

actual.value:
Significant progress was achieved in 2021 with implementation of three training programmes and development of the Edubox innovative classroom project. All partners are in close contact, as we implement the remaining training programmes, developing and deploying the Edubox project. As summary, major accomplishments of the TMT so far includes implementing the needs assessment and three connected training programmes; organizational development (BElink), social entrepreneurship (BElink), and digital economy (BElink). Secondly, design of the Edubox (UT), including technical drawings and engineering specifications is an important achievement of the project. Progress towards developing the project is going well and within the targeted completion and deployment timelines set for the Edubox.
Remaining training activities include, 1) curricula development training (to be organized at the University of Twente), 2) training on gender and psychological issues (BElink), 3) training on developing linkages with the private sector (BElink), and 4) Project management (BElink & UT) are scheduled to be completed in 2022 before the completion of the TMT+ project.

comment.narrative: 3 new facilities established a) learning platform, b) refugee camp self-help unit and c) youth innovation lab (Edubox) for learning and development (targeting youth and women, refugees and host communities

11-04-2023: The Edubox innovative classroom is currently under development at the University of Twente. The design is complete with fabrication (retrofitting) currently underway. We expect the project to be completed and delivered to Yarmouk University before the summer period (June, 2022).
11-04-2023: The Edubox learning environment was developed starting from 01/01/2021 to 31/12/2021 (described in the next indicator).

title.narrative: A.O.2. Number of organisations revised/developed and implemented a strategic plan

comment.narrative: 11-04-2023: This is a long term indicator linked to the training initiatives. We expect the outcomes of the training initiatives and the Edubox innovative classroom to influence education programmes and especially focusing on development of short courses tailored to refugee needs. Furthermore, Dutch partners (University of Twente and BElink) will cooperate to support Yarmouk University and Amel to develop innovative curricula's following the Twente Education Model. The latter is linked to training on curricula development, that is expected this June (2022).

title.narrative: A.O.8. % of women of teaching staff of faculty/department

comment.narrative: 11-04-2023: So far, at least 40% of the ToT's who have benefited from the training initiatives are women. This applies to both ToT's from Yarmouk University and Amel Foundation who attended training on organizational development, digital economy and social entrepreneurship.
11-04-2023: Training of women teaching/faculty staff was realized in 2021 (see description on the next indicator).

comment.narrative: 11-04-2023: So far, two MoU's were initiated with Yarmouk University and the Amel foundation. It envisages cooperation between partners towards training initiatives and the Edubox innovative classroom project. The cooperation extends beyond the TMT+ project and a start towards this end, already the University of Twente and Yarmouk University are cooperating on an Erasmus+ initiative.

comment.narrative: 11-04-2023: So far participants selected for the training initiatives are drawn from Yarmouk University and Amel foundation and are mostly long-term employees, or employees with permanent contracts. To enhance retainment of alumni, partners will be encouraged to develop supporting policies, for instance, engaging trainees as trainers on the long term.

comment.narrative: 11-04-2023: This is a long-term indicator similarly expected towards the end of year 2 of the TMT+ project. We expect the ToT from Yarmouk University and Amel to apply the knowledge to create short courses within digital economy (extending to coding skills), entrepreneurship programs, and organizational development programs.

comment.narrative: 11-04-2023: We anticipate at least 80% of the ToT's and trainees from Yarmouk University and Amel foundation who already participated in three training initiatives as part of this TMT+ will be effective and contribute positively towards training refugees and vulnerable host communities.

comment.narrative: 11-04-2023: The beneficiaries were from Yarmouk University (Jordan) and Amel Foundation (Lebanon). They participated in three trainings, on organizational development, digital economy and social enterpreneuship.
11-04-2023: This indicator was achieved from 01/01/2021 to 31/12/2021 (see the next section).

title.narrative: B.O.1. Number of organisations strengthened by individual and/or group training

comment.narrative: 11-04-2023: All partners, including University of Twente, BElink, Yarmouk University and Amel Foundation benefited from the exchange on knowledge prior and during implementation of the training programmes. For instance, the Dutch education providers benefited through adapting education to tailor to the needs of Yarmouk and Amel. This led to implementation of innovative education delivery, including e-learning and problem-based learning. Furthermore, developing the Edubox innovative classroom is strengthening innovative design-thinking for creating the learning environment (yielded four bachelor projects and one master assignment). Amel and BElink are categorized in the indicator as private organisations, although they are non-government organisations.
11-04-2023: This indicator was achieved from 01/01/2021 to 31/12/2021. See the next indicator.
